hypothesis.statement: The blanket **/*.md rule in .gitignore silently drops new markdown files under docs/ and infra/ because only governance/, .agents/, and tools/remediation/ were ever negated; adding !docs/**/*.md and !infra/**/*.md and tracking the two already-discovered hidden documents will close the gap without exposing any other unwanted file.

intendedChanges: Add !docs/**/*.md and !infra/**/*.md negation lines to .gitignore, following the existing governance/.agents/tools-remediation negation convention.
Confirm via git status that only the two already-known documents become trackable, and re-run a repo-wide ignored-file audit to rule out any other silently-dropped document.
Track docs/MIGRATION_SAFETY.md and infra/docker/PRODUCTION_ARCHITECTURE.md (neither carries a retired/obsolete/superseded marker, so both are kept, not archived).
expectedOutcomes: git status shows exactly docs/MIGRATION_SAFETY.md and infra/docker/PRODUCTION_ARCHITECTURE.md as newly trackable.
forbiddenChanges: Removing the binary/generated exclusions (png/jpg/zip/pdf/etc.) that still apply inside docs/ and infra/.

unexpectedResults: A repo-wide ignored-file audit (comparing git status --ignored=matching against known binary/generated/env patterns) found no other silently-dropped substantive document beyond the two already known; the only other newly-visible ignored paths were .claude/scheduled_tasks.lock (a local runtime lock file) and services/dsh/database/seeds/local/media/** (already-intentional local seed media directories), neither of which is a document.

newFindings: The governance/.agents/tools-remediation negation pattern was scoped to the progressive remediation build's own directories and was never generalized to an audit of the rest of the tree, which is why docs/ and infra/ were missed.
